question:
Consider the following statements about Guru Nanak:

1. He emphasised the worship of one God.

2. He was a contemporary of Kabir.

3. He died at Talwandi in 1539.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Guru Nanak emphasised the worship of one God, and he followed the Nirguna path with no casteism (गुरु नानक — एक ईश्वर की उपासना)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he was a contemporary of Kabir, and both belonged to the Nirguna stream of Bhakti.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: he was born at Talwandi in 1469, but he died at Kartarpur in 1539.

 

• Before his death he named Guru Angad as successor, and he established the Nanak Panth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Nanak's birthplace Talwandi is now known as Nankana Sahib.

 

• The Kartarpur Corridor now links the dera at Kartarpur in Pakistan with Dera Baba Nanak in India.

 

• The Sikh Gurus all came from the Khatri community, a mercantile community.

 

• Nanak's succession plan of naming Angad as heir set the practice of choosing the Guru on merit, and every Guru after him except the last named his own successor.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): The error lies in statement 3, which mixes up the birthplace with the place of death; the pair that includes it with statement 2 therefore cannot be accepted.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statements 1 and 3 retains the wrong place of death, so even though the first statement on one God is sound, the pair fails and omits the correct claim about Kabir.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Going with every statement keeps the incorrect statement that the Guru died at Talwandi; that town is where he was born, while Kartarpur on the Ravi is the place where he died.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Alvars and the Nayanars:

1. The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu, and tradition counts twelve of them.

2. The Nayanars were devotees of Shiva.

3. The songs of the Nayanars are compiled in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Alvars were worshippers of Vishnu, and there were traditionally 12 Alvar saints (आलवार — विष्णु भक्त, परंपरागत रूप से 12)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the Nayanars were worshippers of Shiva, the Shaiva counterparts of the Alvars in the Tamil country.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the 'four thousand divine hymns', is the collection of the Alvars, and not of the Nayanars.

 

• The Nayanar hymns are gathered in a separate Shaiva canon, the Tirumurai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Both groups composed in Tamil and travelled between temples singing hymns.

 

• Nammalvar is the most revered Alvar, and Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar are leading Nayanars.

 

• The Alvar tradition influenced Ramanuja's Sri Vaishnavism.

 

• The Alvars sang in Tamil of the divine joy of Vishnu worship, while the Nayanars performed similar songs for Shiva, so both streams made regional language central.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 turns this pair wrong because the Divya Prabandham is a Vaishnava text; its hymns were sung by the Alvars, so crediting it to the Shaiva Nayanars is an error.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): This choice keeps the faulty statement 3 and drops the correct statement on the Nayanars; the hymns of the Shaiva saints belong to the Tirumurai.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): A choice covering all the statements treats the Divya Prabandham as a Nayanar compilation, which confuses the Vishnu-worshipping and Shiva-worshipping saints of the Tamil region.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Khalsa Panth:

1. It was created by Guru Gobind Singh at the Baisakhi festival on 13 April 1699.

2. Its members adopted the title Singh, and females adopted the title Kaur.

3. It was created by Guru Teg Bahadur to resist Akbar.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa Panth at the Baisakhi festival, the New Year, on 13 April 1699 (खालसा पंथ — 13 अप्रैल 1699, बैसाखी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the Khalsa members adopted the title Singh, and females the title Kaur, which removed caste and surname distinctions.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the ninth Guru Teg Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb in 1675 and had no role in founding the Khalsa, nor did Akbar's reign coincide with the Khalsa.

 

• The Khalsa means Sikh brotherhood, and its aim was to overthrow the Mughals from at least Punjab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Baisakhi remains the festival on which Sikhs remember the founding of the Khalsa.

 

• The first five members initiated are remembered as the Panj Pyare.

 

• Under Guru Gobind Singh the Sikhs fought the Mughal and hill chiefs in several battles.

 

• Gobind Singh set the rule that Khalsa members carry five symbols beginning with K, namely kesh, kangha, kara, kirpan and kachha, which gave the community a visible identity.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 3 (Option 2): Statement 3 stands alone here and is false; the Khalsa was founded by the tenth Guru in 1699, and Akbar had died nearly a century earlier, in 1605.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Joining statement 3 with statement 2 fails because the claim about Teg Bahadur is wrong; the title Kaur and Singh belong to the Khalsa of Gobind Singh, not to the ninth Guru.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Opting for the complete set accepts the wrong founder and the wrong opponent, though the first two statements, on the date and on the Singh and Kaur titles, are correct.

question:
Consider the following statements about Ramananda:

1. He was born at Allahabad.

2. He was the first Bhakti saint to use a regional language to spread Bhakti.

3. He established the Krishna cult and rejected the worship of Ram and Sita.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Ramananda was born at Allahabad (रामानंद — प्रयागराज/इलाहाबाद में जन्म)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he was the first Bhakti saint to use a regional language, Hindi, for the propagation of Bhakti.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: he believed in the worship of Lord Ram and Sita and so established the Rama cult, while the Krishna cult was spread by Vallabhacharya and Surdas.

 

• He opposed the caste system and took disciples from every caste, which gave him a wide following among the common people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ramanandi sect continues his tradition, and its ascetics are called Bairagis.

 

• Kabir and Raidas are counted among his well-known disciples.

 

• His use of Hindi prepared the way for Tulsidas's Awadhi Ramcharitmanas.

 

• Ramananda's emphasis on a personal bond with God, open to all irrespective of caste, directly influenced Kabir, Raidas and later Tulsidas in the Hindi-speaking region.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 reverses the truth: Ramananda promoted devotion to Ram and Sita, and so the pair with this statement cannot be accepted even with the true claim on regional language.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Statement 1 is true, but taking it with statement 3 pairs it with the wrong cult; Ramananda's cult was of Rama, and the pair also leaves out the correct claim on regional language.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Backing every statement given adds the false claim about the Krishna cult, which belonged to the Pushtimarg of Vallabhacharya, to two true statements about his birth and his use of Hindi.

question:
Consider the following statements about Ramanujacharya:

1. He was born in Tamil Nadu in the 11th century.

2. He gave the philosophy of Vishishtadvaita, which challenged Advaita.

3. He was deeply influenced by the Nayanars, the devotees of Shiva.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Ramanuja was born in Tamil Nadu in 1017 AD, in the 11th century (रामानुज — तमिलनाडु, 11वीं सदी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: his philosophy was Vishishtadvaita, which challenged the Advaita of Shankara, and he held that God is Saguna Brahman.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: he was deeply influenced by the Alvars, who were the devotees of Vishnu, and not by the Shiva-worshipping Nayanars.

 

• His Sri Vaishnava teaching set up personal devotion to Vishnu as the path to liberation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramanuja's main centre was Srirangam on the Kaveri.

 

• His chief work is the Sri Bhashya on the Brahma Sutras.

 

• Madhavacharya, who taught Dvaita, came after him and also opposed Advaita.

 

• The Sri Vaishnava tradition built around Ramanuja's thought was centred on Srirangam, and he is said to have also led temple reform and to have admitted lower castes to worship.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statement 2 with statement 3 is wrong, because the saints who inspired Ramanuja were the Vishnu-worshipping Alvars; the Nayanars were a Shaiva group.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Statement 3 again fails here; taking it with statement 1 gives the correct birth period but a wrong source of influence, and leaves out the true claim on Vishishtadvaita.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Ticking all of the statements includes the mistaken claim about Nayanar influence, which contradicts the known fact that Ramanuja was shaped by the Vishnu-centred Alvar hymns.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Bhakti philosophers:

1. Madhavacharya propounded Dvaita, or dualism.

2. Vallabhacharya propounded Shuddhadvaita and talked of Pushtimarg.

3. Shankaracharya propounded Dvaita and argued that the world is real.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Madhavacharya, from the Kannada country, argued against Advaita and taught Dvaita, in which the Jivatma and Paramatma are distinct (मध्वाचार्य — द्वैतवाद)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Vallabhacharya gave the philosophy of Shuddhadvaita and spoke of Pushtimarg, the path of devotion to Lord Krishna.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Shankaracharya gave the philosophy of Advaita, or monism, and the world being real and God, soul and matter being unique is the teaching of Madhva.

 

• Madhva held the world to be a reality and not an illusion, in contrast to the Advaita view of maya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shankara's Advaita centred on Nirguna Brahman, God without attributes.

 

• Madhva's chief centre was Udupi in Karnataka.

 

• Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita lies between the two extremes of monism and dualism.

 

• The three philosophies of Shankara, Ramanuja and Madhva are often called the three great schools of Vedanta, and Vallabha's Shuddhadvaita is a later addition.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 fails because it credits Shankara with dualism, while he taught Advaita; so this pair holds a correct claim on Pushtimarg but is spoilt by the wrong claim on Shankara.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Joining statements 1 and 3 accepts Shankara as a dualist, which is incorrect, and the pair drops the true statement on Vallabhacharya's Shuddhadvaita.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Ranking all three as true includes the mistaken claim on Shankara; he is the monist whom both Ramanuja and Madhva opposed, so he cannot be the propounder of Dvaita.

question:
Consider the following statements about Tulsidas:

1. He was a worshipper of Lord Rama.

2. He composed the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi.

3. He composed the original Ramayana in Sanskrit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Tulsidas was a worshipper of Lord Rama, and so he belongs to the Saguna stream (तुलसीदास — राम के उपासक)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he composed the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi, the Hindi version of the epic story.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Ramayana was written by Valmiki in Sanskrit; Tulsidas retold it later in a language of the people.

 

• He also composed the Kavitavali and Gitavali, and he is regarded as a contemporary of Akbar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tulsidas lived mostly at Banaras and Ayodhya.

 

• The Ramlila performances of North India draw on his text.

 

• Vinay Patrika is a collection of his prayers.

 

• The Ramcharitmanas became so popular that its verses are recited at weddings and festivals in North India, and its story is dramatised in the Ramlila during Dussehra.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 3 (Option 2): Statement 3 alone is false; Valmiki is the author of the Sanskrit Ramayana, so choosing it by itself would be wrong and would also reject two statements that are correct.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Statements 2 and 3 do not fit together since the second is correct but the third credits Tulsidas with the Sanskrit original, which belongs to Valmiki.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Admitting every statement as correct accepts the wrong claim that Tulsidas composed the Sanskrit original, though the first two statements, on Rama devotion and on the Awadhi work, are sound.

question:
Consider the following statements about Sikhism:

1. The word Sikh means disciple.

2. All ten Gurus came from the Khatri community.

3. After Guru Gobind Singh, the Guru was a human successor named Banda Bahadur.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the word Sikh means disciple, and it was Guru Nanak who founded the religion (सिख — शिष्य)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: there were 10 Gurus, and all came from the Khatri community, a mercantile community.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Banda Bahadur was a military commander who led the rebellion against the Mughals; the next Guru after Gobind Singh was the Guru Granth Sahib.

 

• He was executed in Delhi in 1716 on the orders of Farrukhsiyar for refusing to convert to Islam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sikh scripture was given its final form under Guru Gobind Singh, who added Guru Teg Bahadur's hymns.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh died at Nanded in 1708.

 

• Sikh tradition now regards the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal living Guru.

 

• Sikhs regard the Guru Granth Sahib as the living Guru and keep it in gurdwaras, where hymns from Sikh Gurus and from saints like Kabir, Namdev and Ravidas are sung.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): The faulty statement 3 turns this pair wrong; Banda Bahadur was a military leader and never held the position of Guru after the tenth Guru.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Joining the first and third statements retains the false description of Banda Bahadur and drops the correct claim on the Khatri origin of all Gurus.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Accepting the whole set of statements treats a military commander as the eleventh Guru; the Guru Granth Sahib, the scripture, became the successor, so the third statement cannot hold.

question:
Consider the following statements about Guru Gobind Singh:

1. He was born at Patna.

2. He died in 1708.

3. He was executed by Aurangzeb for refusing to accept Islam.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, was born at Patna (गुरु गोबिंद सिंह — जन्म पटना)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he died in 1708, after being attacked and killed by an Afghan.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: it was the ninth Guru, Teg Bahadur, who was assassinated by Aurangzeb after refusing to accept Islam; Gobind Singh's death was by an Afghan's hand.

 

• He founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699, and the Sikh uprising of Banda Bahadur began soon after his death.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tenth Guru was only nine years old when he succeeded his father in 1675.

 

• He is credited with the Dasam Granth, a collection of his writings.

 

• Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib at Patna marks his birthplace.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh's four sons died in the struggle with the Mughals, and he was at Nanded in the Deccan when he was attacked in 1708, shortly before the death.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 spoils this pair, because the execution under Aurangzeb for refusing Islam is that of Teg Bahadur, the father, and not of Gobind Singh.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statement 1 with statement 3 repeats the mistake of statement 3; the birth at Patna is right, but the death by execution belongs to the previous Guru.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Choosing every statement means accepting the mistake of attributing his father's execution to him, which contradicts the death in 1708 at the hands of an Afghan.

question:
Match the philosophers in Column A with their philosophies in Column B.

Column A: (a) Ramanujacharya (b) Madhavacharya (c) Vallabhacharya (d) Shankaracharya

Column B: (i) Dvaita (ii) Shuddhadvaita (iii) Vishishtadvaita (iv) Advaita
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramanujacharya gave Vishishtadvaita, qualified monism, with God as Saguna Brahman, so (a) matches (iii) (दार्शनिक और उनके दर्शन का सही मिलान)

 

• Madhavacharya of the Kannada country propounded Dvaita, dualism of the Jivatma and Paramatma, so (b) matches (i).

 

• Vallabhacharya taught Shuddhadvaita and the Pushtimarg of devotion to Krishna, so (c) matches (ii).

 

• Shankaracharya gave the philosophy of Advaita, or monism, centred on Nirguna Brahman, so (d) matches (iv).

 

• A convenient way to recall the sequence is that Shankara came first in time, then Ramanuja in the 11th century, then Madhva, and Vallabha last, each reacting to the monism of the earlier teacher.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramanuja's work Sri Bhashya and Madhva's Anuvyakhyana were commentaries that opposed Advaita.

 

• The Pushtimarg of Vallabha centred on the worship of Krishna, and Surdas was his disciple.

 

• The Alvars influenced Ramanuja, and the Alvar songs are compiled in the Divya Prabandham.

 

• Madhva's centre was Udupi, where he is said to have founded the Krishna temple, and his Dvaita school argued that the difference between God and soul is eternal and real.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv (Option 1): This pairing swaps Madhva and Ramanuja and puts Ramanuja with Dvaita; dualism is Madhva's doctrine, while Ramanuja taught qualified monism, so two matches are interchanged.

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 2): Here Madhva is given Shuddhadvaita and Vallabha is given Dvaita, which is reversed; Vallabha taught pure non-dualism, and the Pushtimarg, whereas Madhva taught dualism.

 

• a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii (Option 4): This option gives Shankara the label Vishishtadvaita and Ramanuja the label Advaita, so the two are swapped; Shankara is the exponent of Advaita and Ramanuja the opponent of it.

question:
Match the saints/poets in Column A with the works or associations in Column B.

Column A: (a) Kabir (b) Tulsidas (c) Jaidev (d) Meera Bai

Column B: (i) Geet Govind (ii) Bijak (iii) Ramcharitmanas (iv) Krishna bhajans in Brij Bhasha
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kabir is the author of the Bijak, so (a) matches (ii) (कबीर — बीजक; तुलसीदास — रामचरितमानस; जयदेव — गीत गोविंद; मीरा — कृष्ण भजन)

 

• Tulsidas composed the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi, so (b) matches (iii).

 

• Jaidev of Bengal composed the Geet Govind on Radha and Krishna in the 12th century, so (c) matches (i).

 

• Meera Bai composed lyrics for Krishna in the Brij Bhasha of Rajasthan and is popular for her bhajans, so (d) matches (iv).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tulsidas also composed the Kavitavali and the Gitavali.

 

• Kabir lived at Banaras and is a Nirguna saint.

 

• Meera Bai is a Saguna devotee from the Mewar royal family.

 

• Tulsidas used Awadhi, Surdas and Meera Bai used Brij Bhasha, and Kabir a mixed spoken speech, so each saint reached people of the Hindi region in their own dialect.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 1): This option exchanges the works of Kabir and Tulsidas; the Bijak is Kabir's collection of poems, whereas the Ramcharitmanas is Tulsidas's Awadhi retelling of the Ramayana.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv (Option 2): Here Tulsidas is given the Geet Govind and Jaidev the Ramcharitmanas; the two are reversed, since Jaidev's Sanskrit lyric on Radha and Krishna is of the 12th century, long before Tulsidas.

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i (Option 3): This choice assigns the Geet Govind to Meera Bai and the Brij Bhasha bhajans to Jaidev, but the bhajans are Meera's and the Geet Govind is Jaidev's work, so the last two matches are swapped.

question:
Match the Sikh Gurus in Column A with their contributions in Column B.

Column A: (a) Guru Angad (b) Guru Amar Das (c) Guru Ramdas (d) Guru Arjan Dev

Column B: (i) Adi Granth (ii) Ramdaspur (iii) Manji system (iv) Gurmukhi script
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Angad created the Gurmukhi script to safeguard the purity of Punjabi, so (a) matches (iv) (गुरु अंगद — गुरुमुखी; अमरदास — मंजी; रामदास — रामदासपुर; अर्जन देव — आदि ग्रंथ)

 

• Guru Amar Das divided his spiritual empire into 22 Manjis, so (b) matches (iii).

 

• Guru Ramdas founded the city of Ramdaspur, later Amritsar, so (c) matches (ii).

 

• Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604, so (d) matches (i).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gurmukhi is the script in which the Guru Granth Sahib is written.

 

• The Golden Temple was started by Ramdas and finished by Arjan Dev.

 

• Ramdas was the son-in-law of Guru Amar Das.

 

• Together the Gurmukhi script, the Manji network, the city of Ramdaspur and the Adi Granth show how the first five Gurus built Sikhism step by step into a distinct community.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 2): Here the contributions of Angad and Amar Das are exchanged; the Manji system was the work of the third Guru, and the Gurmukhi script was created by the second Guru.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i (Option 3): This option swaps the contributions of Amar Das and Ramdas, giving the founding of Ramdaspur to Amar Das and the Manjis to Ramdas, though each belongs to the other Guru.

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv (Option 4): Giving the Adi Granth to Guru Angad and the Gurmukhi script to Arjan Dev reverses a pair; the compilation of 1604 was by Arjan Dev, and the script was devised by Angad.

question:
Arrange the following Sikh Gurus in the chronological order of their Guruship:

1. Guru Hargobind  2. Guru Ramdas  3. Guru Teg Bahadur  4. Guru Arjan Dev
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2, 4, 1, 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is Guru Ramdas (4th), Guru Arjan Dev (5th), Guru Hargobind (6th) and Guru Teg Bahadur (9th) (गुरुओं का क्रम — रामदास, अर्जन देव, हरगोबिंद, तेग बहादुर)

 

• Guru Ramdas founded Ramdaspur, or Amritsar, and began the Golden Temple.

 

• His son Guru Arjan Dev completed the temple, compiled the Adi Granth in 1604 and was killed by Jahangir.

 

• Guru Hargobind then made the Sikhs a martial community, and after the seventh Guru Har Rai and the eighth Guru Har Krishan, Guru Teg Bahadur was assassinated by Aurangzeb.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Har Rai and Guru Har Krishan came between Hargobind and Teg Bahadur.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth, was the son of Teg Bahadur.

 

• Guru Nanak, Angad and Amar Das preceded Ramdas.

 

• Teg Bahadur is remembered as Hind di Chadar, or shield of India, because he gave his life in 1675 at Delhi to defend the religious freedom of others.

 

NOTE

 

• 4, 2, 1, 3 (Option 1): This order puts Arjan Dev before Ramdas, but the fifth Guru succeeded his father Ramdas, the fourth, so the first two places are interchanged.

 

• 2, 1, 4, 3 (Option 2): Here Teg Bahadur is placed before Arjan Dev and Hargobind, but the ninth Guru lived and was killed long after the fifth and sixth Gurus, in Aurangzeb's reign.

 

• 2, 4, 3, 1 (Option 3): This sequence puts Teg Bahadur ahead of Hargobind; the sixth Guru fortified Amritsar and took the title Padshah well before the ninth Guru's martyrdom.

question:
Arrange the following events of Sikh history in chronological order:

1. Execution of Banda Bahadur  2. Compilation of the Adi Granth  3. Death of Guru Gobind Singh  4. Founding of the Khalsa Panth
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2, 4, 3, 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by Guru Arjan Dev, which is the earliest of the four events (घटनाक्रम — आदि ग्रंथ 1604, खालसा 1699, गुरु गोबिंद सिंह की मृत्यु 1708, बंदा बहादुर 1716)

 

• The Khalsa Panth was founded by Guru Gobind Singh on 13 April 1699, at Baisakhi.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh died in 1708, killed by an Afghan.

 

• Banda Bahadur, who rose in rebellion after the Guru's death, was executed in Delhi in 1716 on the orders of Farrukhsiyar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• After 1708, the Guru Granth Sahib was recognised as the Guru of the Sikhs.

 

• Banda Bahadur's rebellion included the capture of Sirhind in 1710.

 

• The Khalsa members adopted Singh and Kaur as their titles.

 

• The foundation of the Khalsa on the occasion of Baisakhi in 1699 took place at Anandpur in Punjab before a large gathering of Sikhs.

 

NOTE

 

• 2, 3, 4, 1 (Option 2): This order places the death of the tenth Guru before the founding of the Khalsa, but he created the Khalsa in 1699 and died almost a decade later, in 1708.

 

• 4, 2, 3, 1 (Option 3): Here the Khalsa is placed before the Adi Granth, which reverses the order; the scripture was compiled in 1604, almost a century before the order of the Khalsa was formed.

 

• 2, 4, 1, 3 (Option 4): This sequence has Banda's execution preceding the Guru's death, but Banda's revolt came after 1708 and he was executed in 1716, so the final two positions are interchanged.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their birth/period:

1. Guru Nanak  2. Ramanujacharya  3. Tulsidas  4. Jaidev
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2, 4, 1, 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramanujacharya was born in 1017 AD, which makes him the earliest of the four (कालक्रम — रामानुज 1017, जयदेव 12वीं सदी, गुरु नानक 1469, तुलसीदास 16वीं सदी)

 

• Jaidev of Bengal composed the Geet Govind in the 12th century, after Ramanuja.

 

• Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi, and he was a contemporary of Kabir.

 

• Tulsidas, the author of the Ramcharitmanas, was a contemporary of Akbar and lived in the 16th century, after Guru Nanak.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chaitanya was born in 1486, and so was a near contemporary of Nanak.

 

• Basavanna also belongs to the 12th century, like Jaidev.

 

• Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605, and Tulsidas's later works fall in this period.

 

• The Rama cult of Ramananda and Tulsidas and the Krishna cult of Vallabha, Surdas and Chaitanya were the two great streams of Vaishnava Bhakti in medieval North India.

 

NOTE

 

• 4, 2, 1, 3 (Option 1): This order places Jaidev before Ramanuja, but Ramanuja was born in 1017 and Jaidev composed in the 12th century, so the first two places are reversed.

 

• 2, 4, 3, 1 (Option 2): Here Tulsidas is placed before Guru Nanak; Nanak was born in 1469, nearly a century before Akbar's reign, in which Tulsidas worked, so the last two places are interchanged.

 

• 2, 1, 4, 3 (Option 3): This sequence places Guru Nanak ahead of Jaidev and Tulsidas ahead of Nanak in a confused way; Jaidev's 12th-century work comes before Nanak's birth in 1469, so the order is wrong.

question:
Assertion (A): Guru Arjan Dev was put to death by the Mughal emperor Jahangir.

Reason (R): He had helped Khusrau, the son of Jahangir, in his war against Jahangir.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
option_2: A and R are true, but R does not explain A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion is true: Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru, was killed by Jahangir (गुरु अर्जन देव — जहाँगीर द्वारा मृत्युदंड)

 

• Reason is true: he supported Khusrau, the rebel son of Jahangir, during Khusrau's war against his father.

 

• The reason explains the assertion, because Jahangir treated the Guru's help to the rebel prince as political opposition, and this led to the execution.

 

• The event pushed the Sikhs towards military organisation under his son Guru Hargobind.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604, two years before his death in 1606.

 

• Prince Khusrau's revolt took place in 1606.

 

• Guru Hargobind kept two swords after his father's martyrdom.

 

• Guru Arjan's execution in 1606 at Lahore is regarded as the first great martyrdom of Sikh history, and his son Hargobind responded by wearing two swords for spiritual and worldly authority.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are true, but R does not explain A (Option 2): Describing the reason as unconnected misreads the case: his aid to Khusrau was the very ground on which Jahangir punished him, so the two true statements are linked causally.

 

• A is true, but R is false (Option 3): Calling the assertion true but the reason false is wrong, since Guru Arjan Dev really did help the rebel prince Khusrau, so both statements stand as facts.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 4): Treating the assertion as false is wrong because the fifth Guru was killed by Jahangir, not Aurangzeb, so the assertion is true, and the reason supports it.

question:
Assertion (A): Guru Angad created the Manji system of 22 branches of Sikhism.

Reason (R): Guru Amar Das divided his spiritual empire into 22 parts called Manjis for the propagation of Sikh ideas.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
option_2: A is false, but R is true
option_3: A and R are true, but R does not explain A
option_4: A is true, but R is false
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is false, but R is true.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion is false: the Manji system was not created by Guru Angad, whose known work was the Gurmukhi script (गुरु अंगद ने गुरुमुखी बनाई; मंजी प्रणाली गुरु अमरदास की)

 

• Reason is true: Guru Amar Das, the third Guru, divided his spiritual empire into 22 Manjis for preaching Sikh ideas.

 

• Hence the reason is right but actually contradicts the assertion, as it attributes the system to a different Guru.

 

• Akbar visited Guru Amar Das, and the fourth Guru Ramdas married his daughter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Amar Das became Guru after Guru Angad.

 

• Each Manji was run by a Sikh appointed as a preacher.

 

• Guru Angad's original name was Lehna.

 

• Guru Amar Das also opposed practices like sati and the purdah, and he insisted that all visitors eat together in the langar before meeting him, regardless of caste.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are true, and R correctly explains A (Option 1): The assertion cannot be true because Guru Angad is credited with the Gurmukhi script, not the 22 Manjis, so a claim that treats both statements as true and explained fails.

 

• A and R are true, but R does not explain A (Option 3): Taking both statements as true while denying a link also fails; the assertion misattributes the Manji system, and a false assertion cannot be accepted as a true statement.

 

• A is true, but R is false (Option 4): Calling the assertion true and the reason false reverses the facts: the Manji system is correctly described in the reason, while the assertion gives the wrong Guru.

question:
Assertion (A): Chaitanya Mahaprabhu believed in idol worship.

Reason (R): Chaitanya was a Nirguna saint who rejected the worship of images.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
option_2: A and R are true, but R does not explain A
option_3: A is false, but R is true
option_4: A is true, but R is false
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion is true: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was a Saguna saint, and so he believed in idol worship (चैतन्य महाप्रभु — सगुण संत, मूर्ति पूजा में विश्वास)

 

• Reason is false: he was not a Nirguna saint; he considered himself an incarnation of Krishna and Radha.

 

• Nirguna saints such as Kabir, Raidas, Guru Nanak and Pipa rejected idol worship, but Chaitanya is placed with Meera Bai and Tulsidas among Saguna saints.

 

• His major contribution was sankirtan, group devotional singing with dancing, in Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chaitanya is associated with the Nadiya region of Bengal.

 

• He had Hindu and Muslim disciples and did not accept Brahmin supremacy.

 

• His followers are called Gaudiya Vaishnavas.

 

• Chaitanya spent his last years at Puri in Odisha, and his Gaudiya Vaishnava followers later settled at Vrindavan, where they built temples dedicated to Radha and Krishna.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are true, and R correctly explains A (Option 1): The reason is not true, so the idea that it correctly explains the assertion fails; Chaitanya was a Saguna devotee who honoured Krishna's image in worship.

 

• A and R are true, but R does not explain A (Option 2): The reason is not a true statement, even though the assertion is true, so the claim that both are true though unrelated does not stand.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 3): Treating the assertion as false is incorrect, because Chaitanya did believe in idol worship as a Saguna saint, and the reason is the false one.

question:
Assertion (A): Ramananda is regarded as the first Bhakti saint to use a regional language to spread Bhakti.

Reason (R): Ramananda established the Rama cult and believed in the worship of Ram and Sita.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: A and R are true, but R does not explain A
option_2: A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and R are true, but R does not explain A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion is true: Ramananda was the first Bhakti saint to use a regional language, Hindi, for propagating Bhakti (रामानंद — पहले भक्त संत जिन्होंने हिंदी का प्रयोग किया)

 

• Reason is true: he worshipped Ram and Sita and thus founded the Rama cult.

 

• The reason is not an explanation of the assertion; the language he used to preach and the deity he worshipped are two separate facts about him.

 

• The two facts together show that the Rama cult spread to common people through Hindi rather than Sanskrit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramananda took disciples from every caste, opposing the caste system.

 

• He was born at Allahabad.

 

• Kabir and Raidas are counted among his disciples.

 

• The Ramanandi sect, whose ascetics are called Bairagis, is still the largest Vaishnava monastic group of North India, which shows how long Ramananda's Hindi preaching endured.

 

NOTE

 

• A and R are true, and R correctly explains A (Option 2): The reason does not explain why he preached in Hindi, since worship of Rama is the content of his teaching and not the cause of his language choice, so a causal link is wrongly claimed.

 

• A is true, but R is false (Option 3): The reason cannot be called false, because Ramananda did establish the Rama cult, and the assertion on the use of a regional language is also true.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 4): The assertion cannot be called false, as he is the first Bhakti saint recorded as using a regional language, and the reason is a true fact.

question: Which of the following saints is NOT classified as a Nirguna saint?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chaitanya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is a Saguna saint, as he believed in idol worship and considered himself an incarnation of Krishna and Radha (चैतन्य — सगुण संत, निर्गुण नहीं)

 

• The Nirguna list in the notes comprises Kabir, Raidas, Guru Nanak and Pipa, who opposed idol worship and Brahmin supremacy.

 

• The Saguna list includes Meera Bai, Tulsidas and Chaitanya, who worshipped a God with form.

 

• Chaitanya nevertheless rejected Brahmin supremacy and accepted Hindu and Muslim disciples, so his social outlook was liberal even though his worship was image-centred.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nirguna saints mostly came from the lower castes.

 

• Pipa is another Nirguna saint, from Rajasthan.

 

• The Saguna tradition included Rama and Krishna devotion.

 

• Kabir's, Raidas's and Nanak's rejection of caste distinctions made the Nirguna stream especially attractive to artisans, weavers and cultivators in North India.

 

• The Saguna group in this classification includes Meera Bai and Tulsidas as well, and the contrast shows that social origin as much as belief shaped the sorting.

 

NOTE

 

• Kabir (Option 1): Kabir is a Nirguna Bhakti saint who attacked idol worship and Brahmin supremacy and composed the Bijak, so he does belong to the group that the question asks to exclude.

 

• Raidas (Option 2): Raidas is a Nirguna saint who was a disciple of Ramananda and rejected caste distinctions; he is therefore part of the Nirguna group and cannot be the exception.

 

• Guru Nanak (Option 3): Guru Nanak preached the worship of one formless God and rejected casteism, which puts him in the Nirguna group, and hence he is not the saint who is outside it.

question: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
option_1: Guru Hargobind - Compiled the Adi Granth
option_2: Guru Angad - Created the Gurmukhi script
option_3: Guru Har Rai - Free Ayurvedic hospital and herbal garden
option_4: Guru Teg Bahadur - Assassinated by Aurangzeb
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Hargobind - Compiled the Adi Granth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by Guru Arjan Dev, not by Guru Hargobind, so this pair is wrongly matched (गलत युग्म — आदि ग्रंथ अर्जन देव ने संकलित किया)

 

• Guru Hargobind is remembered for turning the Sikhs into a martial community, starting the Akal Takht and taking the title Padshah.

 

• Guru Angad created the Gurmukhi script, and Guru Har Rai established a free Ayurvedic hospital and herbal garden.

 

• Guru Teg Bahadur was assassinated by Aurangzeb after refusing to join Islam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arjan Dev included the hymns of Nanak, Angad, Amar Das and Ramdas in the Adi Granth.

 

• Hargobind also fortified Amritsar.

 

• Teg Bahadur's hymns were added to the scripture by Gobind Singh.

 

• Guru Angad's Gurmukhi script, Guru Arjan's Adi Granth and Guru Hargobind's Akal Takht mark three stages of Sikh identity, namely script, scripture and sovereignty.

 

NOTE

 

• Guru Angad - Created the Gurmukhi script (Option 2): This pair is correct: Guru Angad created Gurmukhi to safeguard the Punjabi language, so it cannot be the incorrect pair the question seeks.

 

• Guru Har Rai - Free Ayurvedic hospital and herbal garden (Option 3): This pair is also correct, since the seventh Guru set up a free Ayurvedic hospital and a herbal garden, a humane act that fits him, and so it is not the odd one out.

 

• Guru Teg Bahadur - Assassinated by Aurangzeb (Option 4): This pair is accurate as well; the ninth Guru refused conversion to Islam and was killed on Aurangzeb's orders, which makes it a correct pairing and not the wrong one.

question: Wahdat-ul-wajud, a belief held by the Sufis, means:
option_1: Visiting the tomb of a Sufi saint
option_2: Chain of spiritual descent from teacher to disciple
option_3: Unity of being - God and creature are the same
option_4: Group singing of devotional songs with dancing
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unity of being - God and creature are the same.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wahdat-ul-wajud means the unity of being, the belief that God and creature are the same (वहदत-उल-वजूद — अस्तित्व की एकता)

 

• It is a central idea of the Sufi mystics, who held that the soul can unite with God through love and devotion.

 

• The idea parallels the monism of Indian thought, which helped Sufis and Bhakti saints find common ground.

 

• The Sufi movement entered India from Persia in the 11th century, with the Chishti, Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi and Qadiri silsilas as the four powerful orders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ibn Arabi is the thinker most associated with the doctrine.

 

• Sufis called their teachers pirs and shaikhs.

 

• Sufi centres were called khanqahs.

 

• Ibn Arabi, the Andalusian mystic, is the thinker most closely linked with the unity of being, and stricter scholars such as the Naqshbandi reformer Sirhindi criticised the doctrine.

 

NOTE

 

• Visiting the tomb of a Sufi saint (Option 1): Visiting a saint's tomb is called Ziyarat, a devotional practice at a dargah like Ajmer, whereas Wahdat-ul-wajud is a doctrine about the relation of God and creation.

 

• Chain of spiritual descent from teacher to disciple (Option 2): A chain of spiritual descent from teacher to disciple is the silsila, which is an organisational lineage, while the term in the question names a metaphysical belief.

 

• Group singing of devotional songs with dancing (Option 4): Group singing of devotional songs with dancing is sankirtan, which Chaitanya introduced in Bengal as a Hindu Bhakti practice and is unrelated to the Sufi belief in the unity of being.

question: The gradual militarisation of the Sikh community under Guru Hargobind and Guru Gobind Singh was primarily a response to:
option_1: A desire to expand into South India
option_3: A pact with the Marathas against Delhi
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mughal persecution of the Sikhs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sikh militarisation was mainly a response to Mughal persecution, which included the execution of Guru Arjan Dev by Jahangir and of Guru Teg Bahadur by Aurangzeb (सिखों का सैन्यीकरण — मुगल उत्पीड़न की प्रतिक्रिया)

 

• Guru Hargobind turned the Sikhs into a martial community, started the Akal Takht, fortified Amritsar and took the title Padshah.

 

• Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa Panth in 1699, whose aim was to overthrow the Mughals from at least Punjab.

 

• After 1708, Banda Bahadur continued the armed struggle until his execution in 1716.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Gobind Singh's struggle also involved hill chiefs of the Shivalik region.

 

• The Khalsa members carried arms as part of their code.

 

• Later Sikh Misls in the 18th century grew from this military tradition.

 

• The Sikh Panth's military character appeared further in the 18th century in the Dal Khalsa, and in the Misls, which later united under Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

 

NOTE

 

• A desire to expand into South India (Option 1): Expansion into South India was never a Sikh aim; the Khalsa's stated aim concerned Punjab, and the fighting was a defence against Mughal power and not an offensive far to the south.

 

• Internal quarrels over scripture (Option 2): Internal quarrels over scripture did not cause the shift; the scripture, the Adi Granth, had been compiled by Guru Arjan Dev in 1604, and the military change followed the executions of the Gurus.

 

• A pact with the Marathas against Delhi (Option 3): A pact with the Marathas was not a cause of the militarisation, as the Sikh and Maratha struggles with Mughal rule were largely separate, and the change began with Hargobind decades earlier.

question: Which Sikh Guru, whose daughter was married to the fourth Guru, was visited by the Mughal emperor Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Amar Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Amar Das, the third Guru, was visited by Akbar, and his daughter was married to the fourth Guru, Ramdas (गुरु अमरदास — अकबर की भेंट; पुत्री का विवाह रामदास से)

 

• He divided his spiritual empire into 22 Manjis to spread Sikh teaching.

 

• The family tie made Guru Arjan Dev, the son of Ramdas, his grandson through his daughter.

 

• The friendly relations with Akbar contrast with the later conflicts between the Sikhs and Jahangir and Aurangzeb.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tradition says Akbar had a meal at the langar before meeting the Guru.

 

• Akbar is also said to have given land for the Golden Temple.

 

• Goindwal on the Beas was the centre of Guru Amar Das.

 

• The Mughal-Sikh relationship changed from respect under Akbar to conflict under Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, as Sikh numbers and political influence grew in Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Guru Angad (Option 1): Guru Angad, the second Guru, created Gurmukhi and was Nanak's successor; no tradition links him with a daughter's marriage to the fourth Guru or with a visit by Akbar.

 

• Guru Arjan Dev (Option 2): Guru Arjan Dev was the fifth Guru, and he was himself the son of Ramdas, so his daughter could not have been the fourth Guru's wife; he was executed by Jahangir.

 

• Guru Hargobind (Option 4): Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, was the son of Arjan Dev and became a warrior-Guru under Jahangir; he came after the fourth Guru and so could not be the father-in-law of Ramdas.

question: Which Sikh Guru set up a free Ayurvedic hospital and a herbal garden?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Har Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Har Rai, the seventh Guru, established a free Ayurvedic hospital and a herbal garden (गुरु हर राय — निःशुल्क आयुर्वेदिक अस्पताल)

 

• He came after Guru Hargobind, the martial Guru, and was followed by Guru Har Krishan, the youngest Guru.

 

• His work shows the Sikh ideal of service to the sick, drawn from Guru Nanak's emphasis on equality and service.

 

• The Gurus after him were Har Krishan (8th), Teg Bahadur (9th) and Gobind Singh (10th).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Har Rai was the grandson of Guru Hargobind.

 

• He is said to have kept a large force but avoided battle.

 

• Kiratpur was his seat.

 

• Guru Har Rai's herbal garden is said to have given medicines for the sick, and he is remembered for kindness to wounded animals, as well as for his help to people of all faiths.

 

NOTE

 

• Guru Har Krishan (Option 1): Guru Har Krishan became Guru at five years of age and died young, so he is remembered as the youngest Guru; no hospital or herbal garden is ascribed to him.

 

• Guru Hargobind (Option 3): Guru Hargobind is known for making Sikhs a martial community, starting the Akal Takht and fortifying Amritsar; the Ayurvedic hospital is not part of his record.

 

• Guru Ramdas (Option 4): Guru Ramdas founded Ramdaspur or Amritsar and began the Golden Temple, but the free Ayurvedic hospital and herbal garden are ascribed to a later Guru, the seventh.
